html:
The Gajirrawoong are an Aboriginal Australian people of the coast around Joseph Bonaparte Gulf, on the border of Western Australia and the Northern Territory, shown on the map as Kadjerong from 1600 to 1815. Most now live in the northeast of Western Australia, around Kununurra and Wyndham.

Their neighbours included the Miriwoong inland, the Yiiji and Kwini across Cambridge Gulf to the west, and the Murrinh-Patha to the northeast. Cattle stations spread into the east Kimberley from the 1880s, and the port of Wyndham was founded in 1886 to serve the Halls Creek gold rush. Their language, Gajirrabeng, is close to Miriwoong and now has very few speakers.
